tasks.short: Monitor rolling cycles for jams and product conformity

steps.what: Observe actual machine cycles, material travel and product condition to detect jamming and visible nonconformity
inputs: actual mill cycles and material
actual product specifications
outputs: operator's observed jams and product-condition findings

steps.what: Read available mill status indicators and existing process readings and compare them with the product specifications
inputs: machine's actual available process readings and status
actual product specifications
operator's observed jams and product-condition findings

tasks.design: Configure the existing mill-status view in {OTHER}, the mill control display, to keep available readings visible together. The operator continues watching material travel and product condition; the view only reduces navigation among readings already produced by the machine.
tasks.previous_blocker: Available control readings may sit on separate display pages.
tasks.enabler_now: Native display configuration can group existing readings.
tasks.still_hard: Jams and actual product defects can emerge before a display makes them clear.
tasks.human_edge: Connect the live material behaviour with the indicators and specification.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native mill display configuration can group existing readings while live jam and product monitoring remain operator work.

assumptions: Shares are provisional human effort, not mill runtime or measured baselines.
OTHER means the existing mill control display. Existing sensors/control produce the actual readings; no new sensing or inferred product-quality data is assumed.
Only display navigation changes. Existing equivalent views, analogue-only controls or unavailable readings give zero gain.
Gross provisional saving 1 minus 0.25 hour of display-setting upkeep gives 0.75 net. No report, send or machine adjustment is introduced by this monitoring design.
research_questions: Can a native view remove navigation while retaining all actual monitoring checks?

already_counted.description: Read and assess actual process readings

incremental.description: Check display settings after authorised control changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Below provisional net 0.75%; direct physical observation remains fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read rolling orders and determine setup and work sequence

steps.what: Locate and read the actual rolling order, current blueprint and mill schedule for the assigned job
inputs: actual assigned job identity
planner's rolling order and mill schedule
engineering's current blueprint
outputs: operator-read order, blueprint and schedule for the same job version

steps.what: Interpret the rolling order and blueprint to determine setup specifications, work sequence, product dimensions and installation procedures
inputs: operator-read order, blueprint and schedule for the same job version
actual mill capabilities and installation instructions
outputs: operator's determined setup requirements and unresolved conflicts

tasks.design: Configure direct job links from {OPS_SYSTEM}, the production-order system, to the current blueprint in {DOCS} and the corresponding schedule. The operator reads the actual documents and determines the setup requirements; no document extractor or automatic setup is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Orders, drawings and schedules may require separate navigation and version matching.
tasks.enabler_now: Native job/document links can expose the existing records for the same job.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting requirements and installation constraints require shop-floor interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when the drawing cannot be executed as written on the actual mill.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native production-order links can expose current drawings and schedules while operators retain setup interpretation.

assumptions: Shares are unmeasured task scenarios, not prompt priors. OPS_SYSTEM means production-order and scheduling software.
Planning produces the order/job identity and schedule; engineering publishes drawing identity and revision. Missing or conflicting links require manual confirmation rather than inferred setup facts.
Only navigation/version matching changes; actual reading and interpretation remain. Existing equivalent links remove the gain.
Gross provisional saving 4.5 minus 0.5 hour of job-link upkeep gives 4 net. This read-and-determine task creates no invented separate report, send or control commit.
unknowns: Existing drawing links and actual version-matching effort
research_questions: Do real rolling jobs require repeated document navigation that native job links can remove?

already_counted.description: Read job documents and determine actual setup requirements

incremental.description: Check job-to-drawing links and revision pointers

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Below provisional net 4%; only repeated retrieval/version navigation changes.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Monitor indicators and regulate rolling-machine speeds

steps.what: Observe the actual dial indicators, machine response and material behaviour while monitoring mechanism speed
inputs: actual speed dial indicators and running mechanisms
actual material behaviour and job requirements
outputs: operator's actual speed and machine-response observations

steps.what: Choose the exact permitted speed-control adjustment from the observed response and job requirements
inputs: operator's actual speed and machine-response observations
permitted operating limits and control instructions

steps.what: Manipulate the controls to apply the selected speed adjustment and observe its actual effect
inputs: operator-selected speed-control adjustment
actual mill controls and mechanisms
outputs: actual adjusted mechanism speed and observed response

tasks.design: Keep live speed regulation with the operator at the machine. Dial reading, adjustment selection and the control action are separate; a native display or recipe cannot be credited with removing them without evidence that the actual mill supports that change.
tasks.previous_blocker: The task is direct feedback-based manipulation of a running mechanism.
tasks.enabler_now: No additional software mechanism is established for the actual controls.
tasks.still_hard: Material and mechanism response require immediate local observation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise unsafe response and choose the permitted intervention.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: direct dial observation and physical speed adjustment require suitable machine control capabilities before software savings can be claimed.

assumptions: Shares are illustrative and unmeasured. Actual indicators are read directly; no new telemetry producer is assumed.
No report, lookup outside the control panel or record write is established in this speed-regulation task; none is invented to create a saving.
The exact selected control action follows the operator's decision. A changed adjustment requires another decision; no hidden automatic commit is proposed.
All actual work remains, gross/net saving are zero and no new upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Actual mill control capabilities and existing closed-loop control
research_questions: Does the actual mill have an approved native control feature that changes this operator work?

incremental.description: No new software or control process proposed

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No verified change to direct speed observation or control manipulation.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Calculate draft space and roll speed for each mill stand

steps.what: Read and check actual entry/exit dimensions, material and temper requirements, roll geometry and mill operating limits
inputs: actual rolling order dimensions, material and required temper
actual stand/roll geometry and approved mill limits

steps.what: Calculate draft space and roll speed stand by stand using the approved rolling method and actual inputs
inputs: operator-checked mill-stand calculation inputs
approved rolling calculations and pass-sequence method
outputs: calculated stand-by-stand draft spaces and roll speeds with input references

steps.what: Check the complete calculated rolling sequence against dimensions, temper requirements and mill limits and resolve exceptions
inputs: calculated stand-by-stand draft spaces and roll speeds with input references
operator-checked mill-stand calculation inputs
outputs: complete checked draft-space and roll-speed sequence

steps.what: Save the completed checked calculation sequence in the existing job workspace
inputs: complete checked draft-space and roll-speed sequence

tasks.design: Configure the approved rolling calculation sheet in {SPREADSHEET} or the existing pass-planning calculator in {OTHER} before building anything custom. It calculates each stand's draft space and roll speed from actual checked inputs; the operator verifies the complete sequence before saving it, with no machine download.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated stand-by-stand calculation or formula setup can require manual arithmetic and transfer.
tasks.enabler_now: Validated deterministic formulas can reuse actual dimensional and stand inputs.
tasks.still_hard: Material behaviour and mill limits determine whether a numerical sequence is usable.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise a numerically consistent but physically unsuitable rolling sequence.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-4 for approved calculation methods and mill/job data access

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: validated rolling calculation sheets can compute stand-specific settings deterministically, with operator review of physical applicability.

assumptions: Shares are an unmeasured human-calculation scenario, not computer runtime. OTHER means mill technical-data and pass-planning applications; OPS_SYSTEM means production-order software.

Planning supplies actual dimensions/material/temper; mill engineering supplies stand geometry, limits and approved formulas. The operator checks and enters these in s1; missing fields stop the calculation.
Existing equivalent calculation formulas or calculators remove the corresponding additional saving. No language-model arithmetic or invented rolling formula is proposed.
Gross provisional saving 22.5 minus 2 hours of formula/reference-data upkeep gives 20.5 net; all final physical-applicability checking remains.
Saving is negligible and fully retained. No control-system commit, download or automatic speed change is proposed.
unknowns: Existing calculator coverage and actual repeated arithmetic effort
research_questions: Can the approved native calculator reproduce actual accepted sequences and exceptions with less total operator work?

already_counted.description: Inspect calculation outputs and check the complete sequence against actual limits

incremental.description: Maintain approved formulas and stand/material reference data and regression-check changes

approvals.approved_version: complete checked draft-space and roll-speed sequence

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Below provisional net 20.5%; only real repeated human calculation beyond current native tools qualifies.
